42879293.text: US is a highly effective imaging modality for the evaluation of superficial soft-tissue masses. The authors provide a practical and evidence-based guide for sonographers and radiologists, particularly those specializing in abdominal and musculoskeletal imaging, on how to optimize sonographic imaging and analysis of such lesions. Presented are best practices in image acquisition, a review of advanced imaging techniques, and discussion of image interpretation strategies, with the goal of improving lesion characterization and guiding clinical management.

42911393.label: Background
42911393.text: Patients with muscle-invasive bladder cancer (MIBC) typically have a dismal prognosis, even after undergoing radical cystectomy (RC). To address this limitation, we constructed and evaluated a preoperative deep learning (DL) model that leverages computed tomography (CT) imaging to stratify MIBC patients according to their risk of postoperative disease progression.

42911393.label: Methods
42911393.text: Data from MIBC patients undergoing RC at one of four institutions were retrospectively analyzed and allocated to training and validation cohorts. A dual-channel information fusion DL model was developed to predict the postoperative risk of progression according to preoperative CT images. Subsequently, a DL-based clinical signature was created by combining clinical features with the DL-derived score. The concordance index (C-index) and area under the curve (AUC) were used to evaluate the DL model's predictive capability, which was compared with the DL-based clinical signature, a clinical model, and a Ki67 model.

42911393.label: Results
42911393.text: In the retrospective cohort of 427 patients with MIBC, the DL score demonstrated favorable predictive performance for disease progression in the validation cohort (C-index: 0.774; AUC: 0.785), and generally showed higher predictive performance than the comparator models in the validation cohort. Using an optimal threshold, the patient cohort was categorized into two distinct subgroups, high-risk and low-risk, with differences in the cumulative incidence of progression observed between the two groups, supporting the model's ability to stratify patients according to progression risk.

42911393.label: Conclusions
42911393.text: The utilization of preoperative CT imaging in a DL framework enabled PFS prediction and risk stratification in patients with MIBC, with potential value for individualized postoperative surveillance.

42925843.label: Background
42925843.text: Perineural invasion (PNI) is a strong predictor of early recurrence and poor survival in intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma (ICC). However, PNI can only be confirmed by postoperative histopathology, and preoperative risk stratification tools remain lacking.

42925843.label: Materials and methods
42925843.text: A total of 190 intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma patients from three centers were retrospectively allocated into training, internal, and external validation cohorts. Continuous variables were dichotomized via the Youden index. Independent predictors from multivariate logistic regression were assigned integer scores, calculated by dividing each β coefficient by the minimum β, to construct a simplified scoring system. Performance was validated using AUC, calibration, and decision curve analysis. Using the optimal Youden cutoff , patients were risk-stratified to evaluate recurrence-free survival via Kaplan-Meier and Cox analyses.

42925843.label: Results
42925843.text: Elevated platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio (>144.43), perihilar location, and disrupted arterial enhanced edge integrity were identified as independent PNI predictors. Each was assigned 1 point to construct a 3-point scoring system. The system demonstrated favorable discrimination with AUCs of 0.870, 0.859, and 0.807 in the training, internal, and external validation cohorts, respectively. Calibration and DCA confirmed excellent agreement and clinical utility. High-risk patients (score ≥ 2) exhibited significantly shorter RFS across the training (hazard ratio [HR] = 4.150, 95 % CI: 2.343-7.350; P < 0.001), internal validation (HR = 3.801, 95 % CI: 1.589-9.093; P = 0.001), and external validation (HR = 3.311, 95 % CI: 1.397-7.848; P = 0.004) cohorts.

42925843.label: Conclusions
42925843.text: This MRI-based scoring system offers a noninvasive tool to preoperatively identify high-risk PNI patients, potentially guiding extended resection, neoadjuvant therapy, and intensified surveillance.

42931993.label: Background
42931993.text: Radioconjugates targeting the fibroblast activation protein (FAP) have been successfully applied for nuclear imaging and are currently under investigation for radionuclide therapy. The aim of this study was to assess the biophysical properties of the 177Lu-labeled FAP inhibitors (FAPIs), FAPI-46, OncoFAP, FAP-2286 and 3BP-3940, and compare them with their 161Tb-labeled analogues. The respective 177Lu- and 161Tb-labeled FAPIs were evaluated using fibrosarcoma tumor cells in vitro and a xenograft mouse model to demonstrate pharmacokinetic equivalence.

42931993.label: Results
42931993.text: The radioconjugates (500 MBq/mL) remained ≥ 96% intact in saline over 24 h, irrespective of the employed radionuclide. The 161Tb-labeled conjugates showed similar logD values, uptake in HT1080-FAP cells and FAP-binding affinities (KD: 0.48-1.8 nM) as their 177Lu-based analogues. The in vitro binding to mouse and human blood plasma proteins was moderate with protein-bound fractions in the ranges of 39-56% and 31-61%, respectively, irrespective of the employed radionuclide. After 24 h incubation, the intact fraction of radioconjugates in mouse blood plasma was ≥ 87% while this was even ≥ 91% in human blood plasma without any differences among the same FAPIs labeled with either radionuclide. In HT1080-FAP/HT1080 tumor-bearing mice, the 161Tb-based FAP-targeting radioconjugates showed distribution profiles that corresponded well with their 177Lu-labeled analogues as demonstrated by dual-isotope SPECT/CT imaging and quantitative biodistribution data obtained at 4 h post-injection (p.i.). The radioconjugates were rapidly cleared from the blood, with < 1.5% IA/g retained at 1 h after administration. HT1080-FAP tumor accumulation reached its maximum with 8.8-20% IA/g at 1 h after injection of the radioconjugates, followed by gradual wash-out to 7.4-11% IA/g at 4 h p.i. and further to < 3% IA/g at 24 h p.i. An exception was the 3BP-3940 radioconjugate which still showed 6.4 ± 0.6% IA/g in the tumor xenograft at 24 h p.i..

42931993.label: Conclusion
42931993.text: The in vitro and in vivo properties of the 161Tb-labeled radioconjugates were similar to those of the 177Lu-labeled analogues. The accumulation of these FAP-targeting radioconjugates in HT1080-FAP tumors of mice was reasonably high, however, as the activity declined rapidly over time, repeated radioconjugate administration may be necessary to achieve therapeutic efficacy.

42961643.label: Purpose
42961643.text: To describe the long-term MRI evolution of hepatocellular adenomas (HCAs) selected for conservative management and to quantify the time to predefined degrees of lesion size reduction after oral contraceptive pill (OCP) cessation.

42961643.label: Methods
42961643.text: In this retrospective study, adults with pathologically proven or imaging-typical HCA who underwent serial liver MRI between January 2010 and December 2024 were reviewed. Up to three indexed lesions per patient were tracked, and lesion evolution was categorized using predefined lesion-level size-change thresholds derived from RECIST 1.1 conventions. In lesions from patients with documented post-diagnosis OCP cessation, time to ≥ 10%, ≥ 20%, and ≥ 30% diameter reduction was estimated using Kaplan-Meier analysis. Primary outcomes were repeated in one-lesion-per-patient sensitivity analyses (largest lesion per patient).

42961643.label: Results
42961643.text: 116 patients (110 women; mean age 38 ± 10 years) with 269 HCAs; median follow-up 6.5 years. Among 174 lesions selected for continued conservative management, 166 (95.4%) were stable or regressed. In an exploratory subgroup of 17 lesions with baseline diameter ≥ 5 cm, all were stable or regressive and 11 (64.7%) measured below 5 cm at last imaging. Among 81 lesions after OCP cessation, median times to ≥ 10%, ≥ 20%, and ≥ 30% diameter reduction were 8.6, 24.3, and 49.9 months (95% CI for ≥ 30%, 36.2-75.1). Findings were similar in sensitivity analyses. Both observed malignant transformations occurred in β-catenin-activated HCA, with no surveillance hemorrhage.

42961643.label: Conclusion
42961643.text: In this selected surveillance cohort, most HCAs managed without intervention remained stable or decreased in size during long-term MRI follow-up. After OCP cessation, regression was gradual, with modest reduction often apparent within the first year but larger reductions frequently requiring several years; findings in the small ≥ 5 cm subgroup were exploratory. Limited early size reduction should therefore not, in isolation, be interpreted as failure of conservative management.

42975643.label: Rationale and objectives
42975643.text: The aim of this study was to explore the feasibility of T2-weighted imaging (T2WI) - based radiomics in preoperative prediction of homologous recombination deficiency (HRD) status in patients with high-grade serous ovarian carcinoma (HGSOC), and to establish a non-invasive approach for guiding individualized treatment planning.

42975643.label: Materials and methods
42975643.text: A total of 133 patients with pathologically confirmed HGSOC who underwent MRI scan (T2WI, T1-contrast enhanced) were retrospectively enrolled in this study. All patients were stratified into HRD-positive and HRD-negative group. These 133 patients (41 in HRD-negative group and 92 in HRD-positive group) were randomly allocated to a training set (n = 93) and a validation set (n = 40) at a 7:3 ratio. Three different models were constructed and evaluated: clinical characteristics only (clinical model); T2WI-radiomics features only (radiomics model); and a combination of them all (combined model). The predictive performance was evaluated using the receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis, and area under the curves (AUCs) were compared using the DeLong test. Calibration curves and decision curve analysis (DCA) were applied to validate the clinical-radiomic combined model.

42975643.label: Results
42975643.text: In the training set, the combined model achieved the best performance (AUC = 0.889; all P > 0.05). The radiomics model achieved predictive performance comparable to the clinical model (AUC of 0.762 vs. 0.790; P = 0.676). In the validation set, the combined model performed significantly better than the clinical or radiomics model (AUCs of 0.853 vs. 0.805 vs. 0.706; all P > 0.05). DCA demonstrated that the combined model achieved superior net benefit across a wide range of threshold probabilities compared with the clinical and radiomics models alone.

42975643.label: Conclusions
42975643.text: Our research demonstrated that the combined model achieved the optimal predictive performance. It is feasible to apply radiomics to predict HRD status of HGSOC patients, which can further assist clinicians in formulating individualized treatment strategies.

43013093.label: Objective
43013093.text: Artificial intelligence (AI) may improve prostate MRI interpretation and reduce radiologist workload, but evidence supporting clinical implementation remains limited. This scoping review summarises evidence on commercially available AI medical devices for prostate MRI.

43013093.label: Materials and methods
43013093.text: PubMed was searched for studies published through October 1, 2026. Eligible devices were cleared by the United States Food and Drug Administration and/or CE marked, with commercial availability corroborated through manufacturer websites. Data extraction addressed standalone AI performance, AI-assisted radiologist performance, workflow efficiency, and downstream clinical impact.

43013093.label: Results
43013093.text: Twenty-one studies evaluating 7 commercial AI systems were included; 17/21 (81%) were retrospective and 14/21 (67%) were single-centre. AI assistance suggested greater benefit for less-experienced readers, but improvements were inconsistent and increased specificity sometimes accompanied reduced sensitivity. Standalone evaluations, outside the devices' approved intended use, showed discrimination comparable to that of radiologists in selected cohorts. Inter-reader agreement and workflow benefits were mixed. We identify three key limitations of the current body of evidence that require thoughtful consideration before routine implementation: (1) incomplete verification strategies, (2) limited determination of workflow benefit, and (3) lack of analyses of cost-effectiveness and patient outcomes, e.g., time to treat or cancer-free survival.

43013093.label: Conclusion
43013093.text: Evidence supporting the use of commercial AI for prostate MRI remains limited and heterogeneous, with inconsistent diagnostic benefits. Prospective comparative studies in real clinical workflows are needed to determine its potential role within the prostate cancer diagnostic pathway.

43013093.label: Key points
43013093.text: Question Evidence for clinical implementation of prostate AI remains limited-most studies are retrospective and single-centre, with heterogeneous populations and reference standards. Findings AI may improve diagnostic performance for less-experienced readers, but gains for expert readers and assessment of workflow efficiency are limited. Clinical relevance Prospective multicentre studies embedded in real-world pathways are needed, together with analyses of cost-effectiveness and patient outcomes.

43019243.text: Myoepithelioma is a rare neoplasm that is usually benign and is most often described in adults. We describe an incidental focus of increased PSMA uptake in the region of the distal phalanx of the great toe in a patient undergoing PSMA PET/CT for initial staging of prostate cancer. While the intense tracer accumulation was initially suspicious for an atypical solitary metastasis, subsequent MRI revealed a well-circumscribed soft tissue lesion. The patient underwent surgical excision, and the diagnosis of myoepithelioma was confirmed. This case highlights that myoepithelioma may represent a rare pitfall in PSMA PET/CT interpretation.

43034193.label: Objectives
43034193.text: To evaluate whether automated carotid plaque quantification on carotid computed tomography angiography (CTA) can serve as an adjunctive risk stratification tool for identifying patients with coexisting obstructive coronary artery disease (OCAD).

43034193.label: Materials and methods
43034193.text: This dual-center retrospective study included 2533 adults undergoing paired carotid and coronary CTA within 3 months. Carotid plaque components (calcified, fibrotic, and lipid) were quantified automatically. In the modeling cohort, three diagnostic models for OCAD (stenosis ≥ 50%) were developed using LASSO regression: clinical, plaque, and integrated models. Performance was assessed by AUC (with DeLong's test), decision curve analysis, and calibration curves, with validation in an internal validation set and a temporally independent validation cohort. Sensitivity analysis was performed using severe stenosis (≥ 70%) as the outcome.

43034193.label: Results
43034193.text: All carotid plaque volumes were significantly associated with OCAD (p < 0.001). Calcified plaque volume (OR, 2.43; 95% CI: 1.95-3.04) and fibrotic plaque volume (OR, 1.37; 95% CI: 1.01-1.85) were independent predictors. The plaque model achieved an AUC of 0.785 (95% CI: 0.761-0.810) in the training set, comparable to the integrated model (AUC, 0.800) and superior to the clinical model (AUC, 0.723; p < 0.001). Performance remained robust in the internal (AUC, 0.824) and external validation set (AUC, 0.813). The integrated model demonstrated good calibration. Sensitivity analysis yielded consistent results.

43034193.label: Conclusion
43034193.text: In this retrospective study, automated carotid plaque quantification on CTA provides an adjunctive risk stratification tool to identify patients at high risk for coexisting OCAD, potentially guiding decisions regarding downstream coronary examinations.

43034193.label: Key points
43034193.text: Question Quantitative analysis of carotid plaque components on CTA may help identify patients with OCAD. Findings A model integrating automated carotid plaque volumes and clinical factors effectively identified OCAD. Clinical Relevance This study demonstrates that automated carotid plaque quantification on CTA may serve as an adjunctive risk stratification tool to guide downstream coronary testing in patients with cerebrovascular disease.

43049893.text: It is important to understand the surgical steps involved in the creation of the external genitalia to effectively evaluate pelvic imaging in transgender individuals after penile inversion vaginoplasty (PIV). This review provides an overview of PIV, correlates neoanatomy with imaging, and discusses imaging evaluation of postoperative complications to guide clinical practice. During embryonic development of external genitalia, the genital tubercle differentiates into the glans penis and the clitoris in the male and female, respectively. The urogenital sinus differentiates into the lining of the male urethra and the lining of the vestibule in females. Importantly, embryologic homology provides a framework for understanding postoperative neoanatomy. Our institutional approach to PIV surgery utilizes the glans penis to construct the neoclitoris, the lining of the urethra to construct the neovestibule, and the penile and scrotal skin to line the neovagina. After surgery, contrast-enhanced CT is generally the first-line imaging modality for suspected acute deep postoperative complications, while MRI is preferred for detailed evaluation of neoanatomy and chronic postoperative complications. Correlating embryologic development, surgical technique, and imaging may improve clinician understanding of neoanatomy after PIV. This may facilitate accurate imaging evaluation of pelvic pathology in transgender individuals after PIV and promote timely diagnosis.
